conviction_note: Small positive: the sell-side revenue model MEI is measured against has been pinned near $238M for three straight quarters while actuals ran $240.5M/$246.9M/$233.7M/$298.1M, and the company's own disclosed FY27 building blocks (data centre $80M->$130M, NA auto $182M->~$200M off a $240.5M Q1 base) imply ~$252-260M this quarter versus a $237.99M consensus - but I have marked that down hard for a 17% five-session run-up on zero news into a 52-week high with +14 vol points of put skew already paid, which is a real fade risk that partly offsets the print itself.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 consensus revenue is $237.99M, roughly 7% below what Methode's own disclosed FY27 building blocks imply for the quarter (Q1 FY26 base of $240.5M, plus the guided data-centre ramp from ~$80M to ~$130M i.e. ~+$12M/quarter, plus North American automotive going from $182M to ~$200M), and the same model was at $238.46M against a $298.1M actual last quarter and $224.57M against a $240.5M actual in the year-ago quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: The estimate is the priced number - what is not priced is that it is structurally stale. Only 6 analysts cover a $668M-cap name and the model has sat at $238-240M per quarter through a period when management raised the full-year revenue guide to $1,025-1,075M (implying a $256-269M quarterly average) and disclosed a +$50M data-centre step-up. If the market had reflected the building blocks, the estimate would have moved with the June guide instead of staying within $0.5M of the estimate that a $298.1M quarter beat by 25%, and Baird ($16) and Sidoti ($17) would not both still carry targets below the $18.71 spot. Note this beat is NOT the recovery revenue repeating: my $252-260M figure excludes recoveries, and last quarter's $298.1M less its $22.5M of recoveries was still a 15.6% beat.
findings.independence: Two independent methods land on the same ~$255M: the historical beat rate applied to consensus (+7.1% in the year-ago quarter, +15.6% underlying last quarter) and the bottom-up segment build. The segment build inputs are corroborated from a separate 2026-06-26 write-up of the Q4 slide deck: https://ph.investing.com/news/company-news/methode-q4-fy26-slides-transformation-drives-60-ebitda-growth-93CH-2466855 . Shares the Q4 FY26 release/transcript document cluster with findings 2 and 3.

findings.finding: Every external datapoint bearing on Methode's two growth lines post-dates the 25 June guide: hyperscaler 2026 capex was raised across the board in late July (Amazon $200B to $220B, Alphabet $180-190B to $195-205B, Meta narrowed up), and GM raised its own FY26 EBIT guidance by $500M on 21 July while running Flint Assembly six days a week from June on heavy-duty pickup demand - while Methode's data-centre number is built only on existing vendor-managed busbar volume with the 800VDC rack architecture explicitly excluded from guidance by management.
findings.why_not_priced: Hyperscaler capex itself is the most-covered fact in the market and I am not claiming it is unpriced. The unpriced part is the specific timing asymmetry in Methode's guide: management set the $130M data-centre number and the $72-82M EBITDA range on 25 June, before those raises, and said on the call that 'when we reference the future technology and the 800-volt architectures, none of that is in our guide.' That means the guide has one-sided slack and the print has no mechanism to falsify the 800VDC thesis that drove the Craig-Hallum initiation - the bear catalyst most people would expect here cannot actually occur at the guidance level this early. If the market had connected the two, the July capex raises would have moved MEI at the time; they did not - the stock only moved on 24 August on a boutique initiation, a month later.
findings.independence: GM's own 21 July guidance raise and the Flint six-day schedule are separate corroboration from a different industry: https://investor.gm.com/news-releases/news-release-details/gm-releases-2026-second-quarter-results and https://www.cbtnews.com/gm-to-add-sixth-production-day-at-flint-assembly/ (dated 2026-03-30, confirming the June 2026 start, cross-checked against https://usautosblog.com/2026/05/18/gm-brings-heavy-duty-pickup-inventory-home-to-feed-hungry-u-s-buyers/ dated 2026-05-18). I have deliberately sized the GM leg near zero because Methode's FY26 10-K shows its largest customer at only 10.9% of sales and the top five at 41%, so the truck tailwind is worth single-digit millions of revenue at most. The 800VDC exclusion shares the Q4 transcript with findings 1 and 3.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26's headline was inflated by $22.5M of non-recurring customer recoveries recognised as revenue, so adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M on 24.2% gross margin sat on roughly $275.6M of underlying revenue and only single-digit-millions of underlying EBITDA; management said recovery activity is 'largely done' and excluded the remaining balance from FY27 guidance, so this print delivers the year's worst sequential optics - revenue down ~15% and EBITDA down sharply from Q4 - into a stock at a 52-week high.
findings.why_not_priced: This one is mostly priced and I am filing it at residual size only, because the +14.23 vol points of 25-delta put skew is exactly what a market braced for a trough quarter after a recovery-inflated comp looks like. The residual that is not priced is the composition detail: the $22.5M is disclosed as revenue, not as an EBITDA add-back, so a reader working from adjusted EBITDA of $26.9M and a 24.2% gross margin will not see how thin the underlying run-rate was, and the ~45% sequential EBITDA decline that follows mechanically will read as deterioration rather than as arithmetic. This is compatible with finding 1 rather than contradicting it - a revenue beat alongside weak EBITDA is precisely what March 2026 printed, and the stock fell 12-15% on that combination.
findings.independence: The $45M negotiated / $22.5M recognised split is confirmed independently at https://ph.investing.com/news/company-news/methode-q4-fy26-slides-transformation-drives-60-ebitda-growth-93CH-2466855 (2026-06-26). Shares the Q4 FY26 release document with findings 1 and 2 - the scorer should collapse this cluster.

findings.finding: Exactly one year ago Methode postponed this same fiscal quarter's release on the scheduled release day - 3 September 2025, having pre-announced 3 September on 21 August 2025 - gave no reason whatsoever in the reschedule notice, and the stock fell 11.4% the following session; it then reported six days later, on 9 September 2025, with a revenue beat ($240.5M vs $224.57M) and an EPS beat (-$0.22 vs -$0.40).
findings.why_not_priced: No preview, no aggregator and no analyst note mentions it - the event simply does not appear in any of the three Q1 previews I read, and it is invisible to the baseline because the baseline's history is empty. It is a fiscal-Q1-specific close-process fragility with a documented 11.4% price consequence, and a repeat would be announced within hours of now. If the market carried it, the front-expiry chain would not be implying only a 7.4% event move on a name whose last three prints and pre-print notices produced -11.4%, -12 to -15% and +23.7%. I am sizing this as an expected value on a low-probability tail, not as a forecast that it recurs; the company filed no NT 10-Q and the 2025 outcome was benign.
findings.independence: The original 3 September schedule is independently documented in the 2025-08-21 announcement at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/08/21/3137529/0/en/Methode-Electronics-to-Release-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2026-Results-on-Wednesday-September-3-2025.html , and the 11.4% decline is reported by a third party at https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/stockstory-2025-9-4-why-methode-electronics-mei-shares-are-sliding-today (2025-09-04). Independent of the Q4 FY26 document cluster.

baseline_tension: My largest finding cuts directly against the baseline - the +14.23 vol points of put skew and the trough-quarter narrative it prices are on the wrong side of a consensus revenue number that is ~7% too low on the company's own disclosed building blocks - but the baseline's 16.5% five-day and 23.9% twenty-day run-up cut against me hard enough that I have discounted a +4.5 raw read down to +1.8, and I note the implied 7.4% event move looks too small in either direction given realised prints of -11.4%, -12 to -15% and +23.7%.
